clusters.advice: All propose a non-destructive in-flight channel between queue (invisible) and interrupt (destructive). #59 and #62 are structural syntheses of #17/#22. Design one channel with parameterized signal intent (nudge, redirect, wrap-up) rather than separate mechanisms. Likely needs harness + agent.run checkpoint support.

All root in msg_q not flushed on interrupt while ctrl_q is (entry.py:546). #60 is the structural synthesis pairing queue governance with locale. Start with #26's simplest flush, then broaden to #24/#27. #60 should integrate both axes together.

Progress emission is tool-call-centric; LLM stalls/errors/retries are invisible. #65 generalizes to phase-aware liveness; #69 adds propagation+attribution. Shared fix: extend _StepCollector/_emit_progress to emit during non-tool phases and clear stale entries at attempt boundaries.

_INTERRUPT_REPLY (entry.py:35-38) is the only non-English system message. #63 frames it as absence of any locale model. Simplest fix: change constant to English. If i18n desired later, establish a message-generation layer uniformly.

#61 identifies conflation of attempt-level retry state with request-level completion state; busy flag lifecycle coupled to _reply retries not complete_task. #40 bundles five concerns — split into separate PRs. Core fix: decouple busy/queue gate from attempt lifecycle.

Three logging gaps: attempt dispatch context (#66), LLM failure causality (#67), progress delivery channel (#68). All enrich existing span events. Independent but share instrumentation patterns — consider a unified event-enrichment approach.
Extends _emit_progress to classify read-only vs write tool calls and surface a files-modified counter. Coordinate with #18/#65 liveness work to avoid conflicting progress signals in the same strip.

#47 (investigation-to-action gap), #48 (steering reliability), #49 (delivery receipt truthfulness) are partly agent-side, not purely harness. #48 overlaps with mid-run channel cluster. #49 may need filesystem-state verification in the harness reply path.
